souza2026overview.summary: Reviews 3D printing of Mars habitats with in-situ resources, motivated by the mass and cost of transporting construction materials.
souza2026overview.abstract: The establishment of a sustained human presence on Mars is strongly constrained by the mass, cost, and logistics associated with transporting construction materials from Earth, making in-situ resource utilization (ISRU) a central enabling strategy for surface infrastructure. Among ISRU-compatible approaches, additive manufacturing (3D printing) has emerged as a promising solution due to its compatibility with robotic deployment, efficient material usage, and geometric flexibility under extraterrestrial conditions. This review synthesizes current knowledge on Martian regolith as a construction feedstock, addressing its mineralogical, chemical, and physical characteristics, as well as the extreme environmental constraints imposed by Mars, including low atmospheric pressure, large diurnal temperature variations, high radiation flux, and limited water availability. This paper critically reviews the main 3D printing technologies and material systems proposed for Martian habitat construction, including extrusion-based alkali-activated binders, sulfur-based thermoplastic concretes, and binder-free sintering approaches driven by solar, microwave, or laser energy. Protective design strategies such as regolith overburden, hybrid inflatable-rigid architectures, and consolidated regolith shells are discussed with respect to radiation shielding, thermal buffering, and structural integrity under pressurization. revista2026architectural.summary: Analyses lunar habitat design strategies of NASA, ESA, JAXA, China and Russia.
revista2026architectural.abstract: Permanent human settlement on the Moon represents one of humanity’s most ambitious architectural and engineering challenges. This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of current lunar habitat design strategies being developed by NASA, ESA, JAXA, China, and Russia for deployment within the next 5–10 years. We examine four fundamental architectural approaches: prefabricated inflatable modules, 3D-printed regolith structures, lava tube utilization, and metabolist-inspired modular frameworks. Through critical evaluation of each methodology’s structural systems, material optimization, deployment mechanisms, and habitability considerations, we identify key design tensions between mass efficiency, radiation protection, psychological well-being, and scalability. Our analysis reveals that while prefabricated systems offer immediate deployment advantages, they suffer from prohibitive launch costs. Conversely, in-situ resource utilization through 3D printing and lava tube exploitation presents long-term sustainability benefits but introduces significant technical uncertainties. We argue that successful lunar architecture must transcend purely functional requirements to address placemaking, crew rotation dynamics, and the psychological impacts of extreme environmental isolation. rames2026trains.summary: Examines problems with a multilateral space resource management regime and public-private activity under the Outer Space Treaty.
rames2026trains.abstract: As governments plan to expand into outer space and private parties continue to participate in space operations, the Treaty on Principles Governing the Activities of States in the Exploration and Use of Outer Space, Including the Moon and Other Celestial Bodies (Outer Space Treaty) has the potential to inhibit any ambitions for all but the most basic exploratory missions. That is because Article II of the Outer Space Treaty forbids national appropriation in space, which calls into question the legality of any infrastructure and land use in space. This uncertainty has far-reaching implications for the future economy of space. Fortunately, a compelling solution lies in the proposal for an international resource management regime that can bring land use on another planet into compliance with the Outer Space Treaty. However, it is important to consider that much of the activity in space will fall within the realm of public-private partnerships, and the aforementioned space regime will present unique problems at the intersection of public contracts law and space law.

fedorova2026criteria.summary: Analyses the need for ESG criteria in the commercialising space industry, revealing risks and regulatory gaps in ESG measurement.
fedorova2026criteria.abstract: The article analyzes the need to integrate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) criteria in the context of the rapid commercialization of the space industry and the global sustainable development agenda. The main risks and regulatory gaps in ESG measurements are revealed. Special attention is paid to the comparison of national regulatory regimes in the USA and in the Russian Federation, as well as international initiatives. The directions of improving the space management system to ensure compliance with ESG standards are proposed.

anon2026establishing.summary: Develops a legal framework step to prevent military escalation in outer space.
anon2026establishing.abstract: Abstract: The militarization of outer space has a deep historical context that began during the Cold War when the United States and theSoviet Union explored space for military advantages, initially focusing on reconnaissance satellites and early missile weaning systems. This article aims to develop a practical step for implementing a comprehensive legal framework designed to prevent the militarization of outer space. A focus is to identify and address a challenge associated with the current legal landscape and propose viable solutions that can adopted by an international community. Engaging spacefaring nations through a diplomatic channel is crucial to building a consensus on the proposed legal framework. A Global organization like theUnited Nations and the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) facilitated negotiating and fostering cooperation among nations. A future direction in establishing a legal framework is to prevent military escalation in outer space and must prioritize addressing current research gaps to develop a new capability. A critical area for future research is advancing technologies to monitor and verify.

dasgupta2026policy.summary: Title only: from policy to proposed legislation on legal challenges in India's space sector.

badreddine2026prohibition.summary: Dissertation examining legality of space mining and legal evolution from prohibition to permission.
badreddine2026prohibition.abstract: This thesis examines the legality of space mining in its entirety, starting from the physical act of extracting minerals to the broader legal framework within which any such act occurs, including relevant commercial and environmental obligations, and questions of State responsibility in outer space. In this research a doctrinal and comparative approach has been taken, through interpreting treaties and national legislation, and relying on travaux préparatoires, books, journal articles, and United Nations resolutions. This thesis, through seven main chapters, answers the following questions: does the principle of the common heritage of humankind apply in space? If not, is there a regime governing the extraction of extraterrestrial resources in space? Is space mining legal under this regime? Chapter 2 demonstrates that the principle of the common heritage of humankind does not extend to outer space; while the central argument of Chapter 3 is that at the time of its conclusion the Outer Space Treaty was best understood to have banned space mining. After answering these questions, the remaining chapters address the evolution of the legal norms governing space mining. Chapter 4 examines whether the Artemis Accords has played a role in the evolution of space mining, while Chapter 5 assesses relevant State practice in this field and concludes that a re-interpretation or a modification of one of the Outer Space Treaty’s central provisions has occurred, such that space mining is now pr

coffman2026ground.summary: Designs and tests a magnetic and electrostatic regolith beneficiation system on the ground and in parabolic flight, producing anorthite-rich feedstock with improved separation under lunar gravity.
coffman2026ground.abstract: We present an end-to-end design, build, and testing, of a regolith beneficiation system under both Earth gravity and simulated lunar gravity. The system combines a dual-stage magnetic separator followed by an electrostatic sieve to enrich high-value minerals from bulk lunar regolith simulant, targeting plagioclase feldspar which spans the solid-solution series between anorthite and albite. The magnetic separator consists of a dual-strength set of N-52 and N-42 neodymium permanent magnets to sort the simulant particles based on their magnetic susceptibility. The downstream electrostatic sieve separates particles by size using a single-phase 50% duty-cycle wave with a peak voltage between 3.0 kV and 6.0 kV and operating frequencies ranging from 15 Hz to 30 Hz. The combined system produces four output streams: concentrated iron particulates, bulk basalt, and two sized anorthite fractions according to a target particle size range. The design objective was to obtain an anorthite-rich feedstock exceeding 70 wt% within a 20 μ m to 200 μ m size range. A prototype unit was first designed, built, and tested under Earth gravity to prove the concept. Then an adapted unit was built and tested under simulated lunar gravity through parabolic flights. Experiments using multiple lunar regolith simulants under both Earth and reduced-gravity conditions demonstrate consistent mineral and size separation, with improved performance observed under lunar gravity. nasanjargal2026kinetic.summary: Assesses kinetic and economic feasibility of autonomous lunar export pipelines to avoid Earth gravity well costs.
nasanjargal2026kinetic.abstract: The primary bottleneck constraining the development of space-based resource extraction hashistorically been the prohibitive energy and financial cost associated with the Tsiolkovskyrocket equation. This fundamental principle of astronautics dictates an exponential masspenalty incurred when lifting propellant out of Earth's deep gravity well to facilitate a return trip.For decades, the global aerospace industry has iteratively refined chemical propulsion systems,achieving incremental gains in specific impulse, structural mass fractions, and stage reusability.However, to achieve true macroeconomic viability and industrial scale, lunar mining musttranscend the traditional launch paradigm. It must transition into a closed-loop, structurallyautonomous system where the Moon's native resources provide the raw materials for both thephysical infrastructure and the export mechanics.

hilborne2026newspace.summary: Examines how NewSpace commercial companies affect military conflict and space security dynamics, as shown in Ukraine.
hilborne2026newspace.abstract: Abstract The Ukraine invasion has highlighted most starkly the direct contribution that commercial space companies can make to military conflict. It demonstrates the impact of NewSpace companies on the security dynamics of outer space, and this marks a distinctive—and recent—change in the complexion of the space domain. Such capabilities were not available even 10 years ago. The innovative and entrepreneurial character of NewSpace is driving commercial space activities to expand and develop in every area of space operations, to the point where they now offer capabilities that were previously the exclusive preserve of the militaries of the Cold War space powers, and these can potentially be provided to a wide user set. This has whetted an appetite in Western militaries to leverage NewSpace capabilities. Nonetheless they are not a panacea, and there are some important aspects that need addressing before there is too great a reliance on NewSpace.

ryder2026reach.summary: Working paper presenting a phased roadmap toward a self-sustaining Earth-Moon industrial economy using established physics and emerging technology.
ryder2026reach.abstract: The Lunar Springboard This working paper presents a phased roadmap for the development of a self-sustaining Earth–Moon industrial economy using established physical principles and currently emerging technologies. Rather than relying on speculative propulsion concepts or hypothetical anti-gravity systems, the framework examines how industrial activity, propellant production, manufacturing, logistics, and settlement could gradually migrate from Earth to the Moon. The paper explores the economic implications of lunar resource utilisation, polar water extraction, oxygen and metals production from regolith, fission surface power, orbital shipyards, lunar mass drivers, lunar elevators, and cislunar logistics infrastructure. Additional sections examine orbital cities, large-scale space agriculture, human–AI industrial cooperation, and the long-term emergence of a permanent cislunar economy. A five-phase roadmap is proposed, beginning with robotic prospecting and ending with a mature Earth–Moon industrial network capable of supporting deep-space transportation and settlement. Economic considerations, technology readiness, risk factors, and infrastructure requirements are examined throughout. The paper argues that the strategic challenge facing humanity may not be how to eliminate gravity, but how to organise civilisation around environments where gravity is already less restrictive. petrucciano2026space.summary: Examines how private law applies to the space economy beyond the public law origins of space law.
petrucciano2026space.abstract: Space law was born within the public legal sphere as a lex specialis of international law: the very first agreements on outer space established all operations conducted there would be executed by States under condition of equality, agreeing no one would claim ownership of outer space or of any celestial body. Although these principles still apply, technological and historical evolutions brought private businesses to operate in space: space law should have evolved by elaborating legal instruments opening up to civil liability and personal rights. Law on space would then be called to adapt to the new conceptual frontier of the profitability of space activities. As may be readily appreciated, that would have meant a significant revolution in the relationship between territoriality of law, the extension of the powers and attributions of the States and of the international organizations by one side and that of private law by the other: a historical opportunity that, to date, appears to have gone unrealised. This contribution consists in a comparative diachronic analysis of the development of space law according to its evolving object, in particular to: identify and define the coexistence of both private and public interests in space activities, analyze the gaps in the evolutionary lines of the legal tools used for regulating these purposes, prospect an innovative possible legislative evolution able to permit a balanced protection of private interest in the framework of the run to

angiolo2026economics.summary: Title only: economics of space activities from an evolutionary perspective.

ong2026evidential.summary: Analyses how later practice informs Outer Space Treaty interpretation when spacecraft change operators and jurisdiction persists.
ong2026evidential.abstract: A spacecraft can change hands without carrying all its legal relationships with it. The new operator may answer to one state while another retains jurisdiction over the object and the launching states remain exposed to claims. This persistence of public authority amid commercial change reveals a difficulty in accounts of the Outer Space Treaty that assign extensive interpretive force to later practice. National laws, United Nations recommendations and cooperation agreements often explain how states perform their obligations. Their contribution to an agreed interpretation depends on the legal understanding that other treaty parties have accepted. This article argues that the available evidence supports broad and continuing supervision more readily than either direct attribution of private conduct or exclusive regulatory succession. It develops that distinction through the relationship between national activities and registry jurisdiction, then examines operational standards and reciprocal liability waivers. Article VIII permits arrangements for the exercise of concurrent authority without making the purchaser’s state the exclusive regulator. The International Space Station cross-waiver goes further by altering specified reciprocal claims, while preserving the treaty relationships outside its scope. vogel2026seductive.summary: Essay criticising zero-emission claims of space-based energy systems and their environmental risks.
vogel2026seductive.abstract: This is Essay 07 in the series "Planetary Climate Management - A Total Systems Approach". Abstract This essay dismantles the "zero-emissions" myth of Space-Based Energy Systems (SBES), analysing the hidden environmental risks of importing non-native energy into an already thermally overloaded biosphere. Operating under a narrow carbon-equivalence paradigm, proponents market Space-Based Solar Power (SBSP) microwave-beaming arrays and optical Direct Solar Reflection (DSR) space-mirrors as "clean green" solutions. However, this framework exposes a profound perceptual blind spot regarding the absolute physical boundary of our climate system: the Top of Atmosphere (TOA) Intercept Disc. By deploying orbital assets to harvest solar radiation passing outside the Earth's natural cross-sectional area and redirecting it downward, these technologies introduce an artificial, net-positive Enhanced Inward Energy Vector. Applying the Second Law of Thermodynamics, the paper quantifies how active microwave transmission frequencies (2.45 GHz or 5.8 GHz) induce severe atmospheric transmission and rectenna conversion losses, directly heating resident atmospheric water vapour—the planet's most potent greenhouse gas—and triggering compounding secondary feedback loops. Stripping away the deceptive green taxonomy of "passive" space-mirrors, the text demands a paradigm shift from Net Zero Carbon to "Net Zero Added Heat". It proposes a radical engineering optimisation: re-purposing aerospace technology

arai2026space.summary: Uses colonial Virginia headright elite formation to critically evaluate space resource law and first-mover advantage.
arai2026space.abstract: This study examines how first-mover advantage was converted into durable elite dominance in seventeenth-century colonial Virginia, using this structural logic to critically evaluate twenty-first-century space resource law. Drawing on a Multilayered Frontier Capital Accumulation Model (MFCAM) that integrates frontier theory, world-systems theory, and institutional path dependence, the study addresses four research questions (RQ1–RQ4). Historical analysis shows how the First Families of Virginia (FFV), preempting land under the 1618 headright system, monopolized power through mutually reinforcing mechanisms of institutional pre-emption, marital closure, and symbolic capital accumulation, thereby converting land capital into political and cultural capital to maintain that dominance. At the same time, the study traces the formation of a lower-white stratum through indentured servitude, post-release landlessness, and racial divide-and-rule policies after Bacon's Rebellion (1676) and shows that elite and lower-class formation were two sides of the same institutional design. A comparison with the Massachusetts Bay Colony suggests these outcomes depended on early institutional choices.Based on these findings, the study conceptualizes a "Space Headright System" (SHS) comprising priority access to institutional design, revolving-door relations between regulators and industry, and the accumulation of legal precedent. zhang2025review.summary: Reviews solar concentration technologies for energy self-sufficiency of deep space missions and planetary stations under extreme environments.
zhang2025review.abstract: Deep space exploration missions and the construction of planetary research stations impose strict demands on energy self-sufficiency systems. Solar energy, due to its abundant availability and sustainability, has become the preferred solution. However, extreme environmental conditions in space – including drastic temperature fluctuations, vacuum environments, high-energy particles, and intense radiation – pose significant challenges to the performance and lifespan of solar energy systems. Concentration technology, which enhances photoelectric and photothermal conversion efficiency by focusing sunlight, is crucial for space missions. This review examines the primary environmental factors affecting the performance of solar concentrators, including solar irradiance, thermal cycling, vacuum-induced outgassing, radiation effects, and impacts from micrometeoroids and orbital debris. The analysis focuses on three types of high-temperature concentrators: Fresnel lenses, Scheffler concentrators, and parabolic dish concentrators. Fresnel lenses are characterized by low cost and simple structure but are susceptible to optical degradation at high temperatures. Scheffler concentrators utilize geometric optimization to improve uniformity of light distribution, while parabolic dish concentrators achieve high optical efficiency, making them suitable for high-energy applications though requiring precise solar tracking. nawa2025china.summary: Analyses China's space programme as an instrument of geopolitical power in the Indo-Pacific 2018-2024.
nawa2025china.abstract: This study aims to analyze how China's space program is used as a strategic instrument in enhancing geopolitical power in the Indo-Pacific region in the 2018-2024 period. Using a qualitative approach and astropolitical theory, this study explores four main indicators: space technology mastery, space resource utilization, international cooperation, and space asset protection. The results show that China has achieved significant progress through the successful Chang'e exploration mission, the construction of the Tiangong space station, and the BeiDou navigation system that competes directly with the United States' GPS. In addition, China is actively forging space partnerships with developing countries and engaging in multilateral projects such as the International Lunar Research Station (ILRS). The exploration and utilization of resources such as helium-3 on the Moon marks a long-term strategic orientation in energy and technology. On the other hand, the strengthening of situational awareness systems in space and the potential for space defense demonstrate China's seriousness in safeguarding its strategic assets. In conclusion, China's space program not only reflects scientific progress, but is also a tool of diplomacy and power projection in the Indo-Pacific.

rasheed2025emerging.summary: Relates neo-colonialism trends on Earth to the future of space law.
rasheed2025emerging.abstract: The future of outer space and space law is closely related to the newly developing wave of neo-colonialism on earth. The increasing impact of major power relations, resource driven agendas and with this transformation in global geopolitics, world has seen populist leaders such as Donald Trump emerge in the United States, which means that much of mankind’s colonization in space will be shaped by these factors that are discretely happening on earth. This paper contends that as emerging geopolitical dynamics and the expansion of corporate entities in space alter the prospects for outer space and space law, there are also new challenges. The historical neo-colonial behavioral patterns on earth have increased the risk of “space colonialism”. Such practices threaten peaceful and sustainable exploration of space for all. The study looks at the weaknesses of current space law, particularly the Outer Space Treaty; resource exploration, the activities of the private sector i.e. non state actors and conflict prevention. It calls for a legal framework which is both robust and accommodating of the increasing participation by private actors, protecting equitable access to space resources and preventing this from being monopolized by just a few. The paper explores the need for international cooperation, innovative public private governance models and new mechanisms of law to manage resources to protect the environment and resolve conflicts. pratap2025lunar.summary: Thesis on producing steel on the Moon from Fe-Si alloys that are byproducts of regolith oxygen extraction.
pratap2025lunar.abstract: This PhD thesis explores how metals can be made on the Moon using lunar soil (called regolith) instead of sending materials from the Earth which is extremely expensive. Oxygen extraction from the lunar regolith inevitably produces iron silicon (Fe-Si) alloys as byproducts. This research focuses on first making the Fe-Si alloys from lunar regolith stimulant and then refining these alloys into "Lunar steel". Through thermodynamic modelling and laboratory experiments, the study demonstrated how "Lunar Steel" could be produced by refining of Fe-Si alloys. The resulting strong, ductile steel could support lunar bases, pipelines, and machinery, paving the way for sustainable lunar habitat.

kothalkar2025neuro.summary: Proposes generative design for additive manufacturing of replacement parts off-world to avoid prohibitive launch penalties.
kothalkar2025neuro.abstract: The establishment of permanent, self-sustaining off-world human outposts across the Moon, Mars, and deep-space orbital habitats is fundamentally constrained by terrestrial supply-chain logistics. Delivering structural replacement components from Earth incurs prohibitive economic and energetic launch penalties, ranging from USD 2,500/kg for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) to exceeding USD 140,000/kg for Martian surface descent. In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) combined with off-world Additive Manufacturing (AM) offers the sole viable architecture for deep-space logistical sovereignty. However, contemporary Computer-Aided Design (CAD) paradigms and topology optimization algorithms remain inextricably biased by Earth's 1G gravitational baseline. Structural components engineered for terrestrial environments incorporate massive, superfluous structural material to withstand gravity-induced self-weight bending and hydrostatic settling, resulting in severe mass inefficiencies when deployed in fractional-gravity or microgravity regimes. fallahiarezoodar2025review.summary: Reviews autonomous space robotic manipulators for satellite repair, refuelling, upgrades and debris removal.
fallahiarezoodar2025review.abstract: The increasing demand for on-orbit servicing (OOS) tasks, such as satellite repair, space debris removal, refueling, and upgrades, has driven the need for advanced robotic systems capable of autonomous and precise operations in space. At the core of these tasks are unmanned spacecraft equipped with robotic manipulators designed to execute critical capture and manipulation maneuvers. This paper presents a comprehensive review of space robotic missions and methodologies for effective OOS and space debris removal. It examines control strategies applied across different phases of these missions, with a focus on their implementation in 2 operational modes: free-floating and free-flying. Detailed discussions are provided on methodologies for the pre-capture phase, covering both motion planning and vision-based estimation. For the post-capture phase, the paper explores control methods designed to stabilize captured targets. Additionally, it investigates ground verification experiments, which are crucial for validating the performance of space robots under microgravity-like conditions. These experiments yield valuable insights into the dynamic behavior of space robotic systems and play an important role in advancing space robotics research. By consolidating recent advancements and identifying key technological gaps, this review highlights future research directions aimed at improving the reliability, adaptability, and safety of robotic manipulators in addressing the challenges of OOS

shahrukh2025space.summary: Examines how space technology reshapes cross-domain deterrence as space becomes a strategic arena.
shahrukh2025space.abstract: Space is no longer a zero-sum game domain but the strategic arena of competition in which deterrence is determined not by threatening force but also by controlling orbital facilities, cyber space, and AI-powered decision systems. The evolution of space technologies from precision-strike satellites to autonomous ISR capabilities has rearranged the battlespace with information dominance and disruption being more valuable than sheer military might. The war of today is not mass mobilisation but network centric warfare (NCW), where the key to success lies in controlling the intelligence stream, jamming adversary’s communications, and pre empting attacks before the first shot has been fired. This study analyses how these advances have propelled Cross Domain Deterrence (CDD) - a theory of deterrence no longer based on brute power but on multi-domain pre emption, strategic deception, and systemic vulnerability. Based on a mixed-methods approach, integrating doctrinal analysis, strategic stability modelling, and case studies, this study examines how space and cyber technologies raise crisis instability, encourage first-strike tendency, and erode conventional deterrence mechanisms. Findings show that reliance on AI-based command infrastructure, cyber-physical sabotage, and dual-use commercial-military resources renders deterrence less stabilising and more escalatory. mo2024conceptualizing.summary: Conceptualizes space environmental sustainability in light of in-space servicing, assembly and manufacturing advances.
mo2024conceptualizing.abstract: Abstract Recent advancements have significantly enhanced the capabilities for in-space servicing, assembly, and manufacturing (ISAM), to develop infrastructure in orbit and on the surface of celestial bodies. This progress is a departure from the traditional sustainability paradigm focused solely on Earth, highlighting the urgent need to define and operationalize the concept of “space sustainability” along with the development of an evaluation framework. The expansion of human activity into space, particularly in low-earth orbit, cis-lunar space, and beyond, underscores the critical importance of considering sustainability implications. Leveraging space resources offers economic growth and sustainable development opportunities, while reducing pressure on Earth’s ecosystems. This paradigm shift requires responsible and ethical utilization of space resources. A space sustainability assessment framework is essential for guiding ISAM capabilities, operations, missions, standards, and policies. This paper introduces an initial framework encompassing (1) pollution, (2) resource depletion, (3) landscape alteration, and (4) space environmental justice, with potential metrics (resources use and emissions, midpoint, and endpoint indicators) to measure impacts in the four domains.

losch2024history.summary: Discusses the history, concepts and challenges of proposing an 18th UN Sustainable Development Goal related to space.
losch2024history.abstract: The UN launched in 2015 17 Sustainable Development Goals as part of their 2030 agenda which covered almost every aspect of human civilization on Earth. Outer Space, however, was omitted from the considerations. There hence have already been a couple of suggestions of an 18th SDG related to Space. The paper will discuss the history and motivations of these suggestions, compare the conceptual frameworks provided, and attempts at exploring the structure of the SDGs and such a potential SDG in particular, as well as the challenges that come with that concept. Comparisons are made to the UN Space2030 agenda.

catapult2024illuminating.summary: Argues space-based solar power is a cornerstone of the new space economy, citing recent UK demonstration efforts.
catapult2024illuminating.abstract: The realisation of space-based solar power (SBSP) will be a transformative milestone for the economy, technology and environment in both space and on Earth in the next two decades. Recent advancements and ongoing efforts at the Satellite Applications Catapult and Space Solar have demonstrated that SBSP is not just a futuristic concept but a near-term possibility. Here we aim to shed light on the ecosystem opportunities that SBSP can unlock within the emerging new space economy, based on our work. Realising the benefits of SBSP will require cross-sector and international collaboration, to navigate the unique challenges and issues associated with this groundbreaking endeavour. Keywords: Space-based Solar Power; In-space Economy

langston2024legal.summary: Examines legal and ethical challenges of satellite proliferation and dark sky preservation.
langston2024legal.abstract: The proliferation of satellites in Earth’s orbit has significantly enhanced capabilities in communication, Earth observation, and scientific research. However, this rapid expansion presents considerable legal and ethical challenges, particularly regarding the preservation of dark and quiet skies. As low Earth orbit becomes increasingly congested, the implications for astronomical observation, environmental integrity, and cultural heritage require critical examination. This presentation provides an interdisciplinary perspective on the legal, practical and ethical considerations essential for preserving dark and quiet skies. It begins by exploring the legal frameworks governing the use of space, highlighting relevant international treaties, national responsibilities, and emerging issues aimed at mitigating light and noise pollution from space. The Outer Space Treaty of 1967 establishes that outer space shall be used for peaceful purposes and in the interests of all countries. However, the growing number of satellites and constellations threatens this principle by obstructing astronomical observations and diminishing the visibility of stars—an impact with profound implications for science, culture, and the well-being of all life on Earth. While some environmental laws exist, there is currently no law that adequately addresses the conflict of interests between space activities and terrestrial needs. kilpin2024leveraging.summary: Discusses leveraging AI and blockchain for extracting resources from celestial bodies.
kilpin2024leveraging.abstract: Space mining is a pioneering concept that involves extracting valuable resources from celestial bodies, such as asteroids, moons, and planets. This innovative approach holds immense potential for addressing earth resource shortages and supporting future space exploration endeavours. As humanity looks beyond our planet for sustainable solutions, space mining has emerged as a key frontier, offering a unique opportunity to tap into our solar system’s vast wealth of resources. This chapter draws on prior research in the context of terrestrial mining to consider how the implementation of blockchain can introduce immutability to the management of data related to the ownership and productivity of mining. The chapter contends that the same principles of immutability can also be leveraged to explore new areas of space mining to enhance confidence in ownership through clear celestial demarcations and encourage investment through robust assessment of the productivity of extraction activities, thereby overcoming challenges and disputes that have historically shaped mining endeavours on earth.

shoemaker2024mapping.summary: Tests ground-penetrating radar for mapping buried ice at an Iceland volcano as an analogue for Martian ISRU prospecting.
shoemaker2024mapping.abstract: Abstract Eruptions of the Askja Volcano in Northern Iceland in 1875 and 1961 blanketed the caldera with rhyolitic and basaltic tephra deposits, respectively, which preserved layers of seasonal snowpack as massive ice. Askja serves as an operational and geophysical analog to test ground‐penetrating radar field and analysis techniques for in situ resource utilization objectives relevant to the martian and lunar environments. We conducted ground‐penetrating radar surveys at center frequencies of 200, 400, and 900 MHz to map the thickness and extent of tephra deposits and underlying massive ice at three caldera sites. We identified up to 1 m of tephra preserving up to 4.4 m of massive ice. We measured the real dielectric permittivity of the overlying tephra and the total attenuation at each frequency of the tephra and ice. A key objective of our investigation was to determine if attenuation (or loss) could be used as an additional diagnostic signature of massive ice preserved at depth when compared to ice‐free stratigraphy. Loss rates of the ice‐rich subsurface decrease with increasing ice thickness relative to the overburden, which may constitute a possible signature. Attenuation also increased with increasing frequency.
